questions.question_prompt: Why can a bridge freeze before nearby road sections?

questions.teaching_excerpt: A bridge is exposed to cold air above and below. That exposure can cool it faster than neighbouring road supported by ground, so moisture can freeze on the bridge while the approach still appears clear. Near-zero air alone does not prove ice, but it calls for attention to surface conditions, more space and lower speed. questions.question_prompt: Your car starts aquaplaning. What is the appropriate response?
questions.keyed_answer: Ease off the accelerator and avoid abrupt steering or braking.
questions.teaching_excerpt: ease off the accelerator, keep steering steady and avoid abrupt steering or hard braking. Make only gentle necessary corrections as contact returns. This is different from M02-L01's ABS emergency-stop instruction: ABS cannot create grip where a tyre is separated from the road by water. An immediate collision emergency needs action appropriate to the actual situation; this advice does not establish a universal ban on braking. PennDOT: aquaplaning response Worked grip comparison. A rear slide swinging the tail outward is oversteer; a front slide that prevents the intended curve is understeer. A light, unresponsive steering feel over standing water raises a different possibility: aquaplaning. Recognise the mechanism, preserve margins and practise vehicle-specific emergency handling only with suitable instruction.
questions.coverage_reasoning: Both essential responses: gradual accelerator release and avoiding abrupt steering/braking, with gentle necessary corrections. Cross-link to M02-L01 ABS and scope excludes universal never-brake instruction.
